copyright: Butte at sunset, Face Canyon, Lake Powell, Utah, USA (© Jeff Foott/Minden)
description: Hidden among the maze-like sandstone cliffs of southern Utah, Face Canyon offers a striking glimpse into the dramatic landscapes that define Lake Powell, one of the largest human-made lakes in North America. Formed after the construction of the Glen Canyon Dam, the lake transformed once-isolated canyons into waterways that can now be explored by boat, kayak or paddleboard. Towering red rock walls rise above deep blue waters, creating scenery that feels both rugged and serene. Whether arriving at sunset as golden light paints the canyon walls or seeking shade from the midday desert heat, visitors quickly discover that the journey through this remarkable landscape is every bit as rewarding as the destination itself.

copyright: Rainbow Falls on the Wailuku River, Hilo, Hawaii, USA (© Peter Unger/Getty Images)
description: Water, sunlight and lush greenery come together at Rainbow Falls in Hilo, on Hawaii's Big Island. Here, the Wailuku River plunges around 24 metres over a lava ledge, sending mist into the air as it reaches the pool below. On sunny mornings, that mist can catch the light and produce the colourful rainbows that gave the falls their name. Known in Hawaiian as Waiānuenue, meaning 'rainbow water', this striking waterfall is surrounded by tropical vegetation and has a special place in Hawaiian legend.

copyright: Sunset Point, Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah, USA (© Colin D. Young/Alamy)
description: Snow transforms Bryce Canyon National Park, blanketing the landscape in white while its fiery orange-red hoodoos rise above the snowy terrain. Seen from Sunset Point, one of the park's most famous overlooks, these fantastical shapes are part of the Claron Formation, whose limestone was deposited about 50 million years ago and later shaped by weathering and erosion. Because much of the park rises above 2,440 metres, snow can arrive as early as October. In today's image, snow clings to the canyon's ridges and spires while mist drifts across the cliffs, creating an iconic winter scene in the American Southwest.

copyright: Red squirrel in Cairngorms National Park, Highlands, Scotland (© Scotland: The Big Picture/Minden Pictures)
description: As Britain's only native squirrel species, red squirrels thrive in Scotland's Cairngorms National Park. An important refuge, the park offers ancient Caledonian pine forests and newer conifer woodlands, with plentiful habitat and food for squirrels foraging for Scots pine seeds, nuts and other tasty morsels year-round. In today's image, a red squirrel is perched amid warm orange and yellow leaves, looking right at home as it ponders its next move in the Scottish Highlands.

Today's image shows the gradual coiling of a young fiddlehead's tip, echoing the geometric patterns seen throughout nature. In math, the Fibonacci sequence follows a similar progression, each number formed by adding the two before it: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and so on. Today is Fibonacci Day, celebrated on November 23 because the date's numbers (11, 23) reflect the sequence. Eventually the young fern frond shown here will unfurl as it grows, but elsewhere in the plant world, the sequence will continue to appear in the spiralling arrangements of sunflower heads, pinecones, succulents and pineapples.

copyright: The chapel and hermitage of Santa Justa in Cantabria, Spain (© Tramont_ana/Getty Images)
description: Tucked into the cliffs of northern Spain's rugged coastline, the 16th-century Hermitage of Santa Justa seen in today's image overlooks the crashing waves of the Cantabrian Sea. Built partly into the rock and associated with relics of Saints Justa and Rufina, the small chapel eventually became a pilgrimage site, its sheltered stone walls creating a remarkable contrast with the powerful waves and rocky cliffs surrounding it.

copyright: Nice, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France (© Siripong Kaewla-iad/Getty Images)
description: Bathed in a sun-kissed glow, Nice is a patchwork of terracotta rooftops, historic churches and pastel façades along the French Riviera, as seen in today's image. Founded by ancient Greeks and long connected to the Italian royal House of Savoy, Nice officially became part of France in 1860. Today, that layered past remains visible throughout the coastal city in the south of France, where old-world architecture meets the blue Mediterranean waters and sunlit hills of the Côte d'Azur.
